name.description: The prefix of the rules: `<name>/<rule>`. It replaces the `meta.name` of the plugin.

specifier.description: A path or a package name.

CircularFolder.description: One entry of `folders`: the folders whose dependencies on each other the rule checks.

path.description:
Globs of the folders. `{name}` captures a path segment. A module below a matching folder
belongs to it. A glob matches only the folder it names.

ConventionFilter.description:
Which conventions a rule takes into account: `true` (all, the default), `false` (none) or the
names of the ones to use.

FolderStructureFolder.description: One entry of `folders`: the folders it matches and the checks for each of them.

allow.description:
Globs of the names that the files and folders directly in the folder can have.
A glob that starts with `!` forbids a name. A list of only such globs allows every other name.

case.description:
The case that the names of the files and folders directly in the folder must have.
The rule checks the name before its first `.`, so `Button.test.tsx` is checked as `Button`.

message.description: Oxcruise shows this text instead of the generic message of the violations of this entry.

path.description:
Globs of the folders to check. `{name}` captures a path segment, and `require` and `allow`
can use the capture. A glob matches only the folder it names.
A glob can also match a file. Then the checks apply to the folder of the file.

require.description:
Globs of the files and folders that must be in the folder. A glob is relative to the
folder and can contain `/`. Each glob needs a match.

ForbidRule.description:
A dependency that the project does not allow.
An import from a module that matches `from` to a target that matches `to` is a violation.

from.description: Globs of the importing module. `{name}` captures a path segment, and `to` can use the capture.

message.description: Why the dependency is forbidden. Oxcruise shows it instead of the generic message.

name.description: The name of the rule. Reports and `overrides` use it.

to.description: The target of the dependency: globs, or an object with conditions.

anyOf.description:
A path, such as `"./tools/acme.ts"`, or a package name, such as `"acme"`.
For a package name, oxcruise tries `oxcruise-plugin-acme` first and then `acme`.
An object with the specifier of the plugin and the prefix of its rules.

JsPlugin.description: A JS or TS plugin: a path or package name, or an object that also gives the prefix of its rules.

Level.description: The level of a rule. `off` disables the rule, `warn` reports violations as warnings, and `error` reports them as errors.

ModuleKind.description: What a module is. The names are the ones the config (`to.kind`), the JSON and plugins use.

oneOf.description: A file of the project, parsed.
A file inside `node_modules`: resolved, not parsed.
An import that could not be resolved.

Override.description: Changes the settings of rules for some modules.

files.description: Globs of the importing modules that this override applies to.

Relation.description: How two modules relate, for the `relation` condition.

oneOf.description: `to` is in the same folder as `from`.
`to` is below the parent folder of `from`.
`to` is in a sibling folder of `from`'s folder.
`to` is in the same workspace package as `from`.
`to` is in another workspace package than `from`.

conditions.description:
Export and import condition names. Oxcruise tries them before `import`, `require`, `node` and `default`.
For example, use `["source"]` to resolve workspace packages to their source.

tsconfig.description: The tsconfig for every file. By default, each file uses the nearest tsconfig.

RuleEntry.description: The setting of a rule: a level, or an object with a `level` and the options of the rule.

Rules.description: The built-in and plugin rules, by name. A rule listed here wins over its category.

folders.description:
Entries for cycles between folders. Each entry has a `path`. A dependency from a module in
one folder to a module in another folder of the same entry is a dependency between the
folders. A cycle between two or more of them is a violation. The limit
`maxCyclesPerComponent` applies to the dependencies between folders as well.

ignore.description: Globs of modules to leave out before looking for cycles, so no cycle goes through them.

includeTypeOnly.description:
Also report cycles that exist only through type-only imports (`import type`).
By default only cycles that exist at runtime are reported.

maxCyclesPerComponent.description:
How many dependencies of one strongly connected component are searched for their shortest
cycle (default 100); `0` removes the limit. Several of them can share one cycle.

circular-dependencies.description: Reports dependencies that are part of a circular chain of imports. The message shows the shortest cycle through each dependency.

cross-package-relative-dependencies.description: Reports relative imports that reach into another workspace package, for example `../other-package/src/x`.

dependencies-on-tests.description: Reports a non-test module that imports a test file or a test directory. Test files match `*.test.*` or `*.spec.*`. Test directories are `test`, `tests`, `__tests__` and `__mocks__`.

deprecated-dependencies.description: Reports imports of deprecated Node.js built-in modules and deprecated npm packages.

prod.description: Globs of production code. Defaults to `src`, `app`, `lib` and `packages/*/src`.

test.description: Globs of test code, exempt from the rule (on top of `*.test.*`, `*.spec.*` and test directories).

dev-dependencies-in-production.description: Reports a production module that imports a package from `devDependencies` only.

duplicate-packages.description: Reports a package that more than one `package.json` section declares, for example both `dependencies` and `devDependencies`. The rule ignores type-only imports.

folders.description: The folders to check. When several entries match one folder, all of them apply.

folder-structure.description: Checks the shape of the file tree: the files that a folder must have, the names that it can have, and the case of its names. The rule looks at all files in the entry folders, not only at modules. For the folders above the entry folders, such as the root folder, it knows their own files and folders, but not what is inside the other folders. It does not check those other folders.

allow.description:
Layer name to the layers it may import. A layer missing here is unrestricted.
Importing within the same layer is always allowed.

layers.description: Layer name to the paths it contains. Layers should not overlap; if they do the first by name wins.
Enforces a layered architecture: a layer can import only the layers that `allow` lists for it. The rule checks dependencies on local modules. Packages and built-in modules have no layer.

optional-dependencies.description: Reports use of optional dependencies. An install can skip an optional dependency, so the package may not exist at runtime.

ignore.description:
Globs of modules that are never reported, on top of the defaults
(`**/.*`, `**/*.d.ts`, `**/tsconfig*.json`, `**/*.config.*`).

orphan-modules.description: Reports modules that no other module imports and that import no module.

peer-dependencies.description: Reports use of peer dependencies. The consuming project must provide a peer dependency.

undeclared-packages.description: Reports imports of installed npm packages that no `package.json` section declares.

ignore.description:
Globs of imports that are allowed to be unresolvable. An import is skipped when its
specifier (`virtual:icons`) or the importing module's path matches.

unresolved-dependencies.description: Reports an import that oxcruise cannot resolve to a file or a package.

conventions.description: Which tool conventions count as entry points: `true` (all, the default), `false`, or names.

entries.description:
Globs of modules whose exports are public API, on top of the entry points oxcruise finds:
modules nothing imports, and the files `package.json` points to.

ignore.description: Globs of modules that are never reported.

ignoreExportsUsedInFile.description: Do not report an export that the file itself uses.

includeEntryExports.description: Also report unused exports of entry points, checking them against their importers only.

members.description: Report unused members of exported enums and namespaces (default `true`).

production.description:
Production mode: tests neither are entry points nor use anything, so an export used only
by tests is reported.

test.description: Globs of test modules, on top of `*.test.*`, `*.spec.*` and test directories.

types.description: Report unused types and interfaces too (default `true`).

unused-exports.description: Reports exports that no other module imports. The rule also reports:

conventions.description: Which tool conventions count as entry points: `true` (all, the default), `false`, or names.

entries.description:
Globs of entry points, on top of the ones oxcruise finds (`package.json` entry files, the
conventions of the tools you use, `index`, `main` and `cli` files, plugins).

ignore.description:
Globs of modules that are never reported, on top of the defaults
(`**/.*`, `**/*.d.ts`, `**/*.config.*`).

production.description:
Production mode: tests are not entry points and are not reported, so a module that only
tests use is reported.

test.description: Globs of test modules, on top of `*.test.*`, `*.spec.*` and test directories.

unused-modules.description: Reports source modules that no path from an entry point reaches.

conventions.description:
Whether packages that the tools you use load by name count as used (`@vitest/*` with
`vitest`): `true` (all, the default), `false`, or the names of the conventions to use.

ignore.description: Globs of package names that are never reported.

production.description: Production mode: `devDependencies` are not checked and tests do not use anything.

sections.description:
The `package.json` sections to check (default `dependencies`, `peerDependencies` and
`optionalDependencies`; `devDependencies` are mostly tools that are never imported).

test.description: Globs of test modules, on top of `*.test.*`, `*.spec.*` and test directories.

unused-packages.description: Reports a package that a `package.json` declares and that none of its modules imports.

folders.description: The folders to check. The rule does nothing without them.

visibility.description: Restricts what a folder shows to the code outside it. A module inside a folder can import every module in that folder. A module outside it can import only the modules that the folder makes visible. The rule checks dependencies on local modules.

ToCondition.description: Conditions on the dependency and the module it points to.

kind.description:
What the dependency points to. A dependency matches when it has any of these kinds.
By default, every kind matches, except for `reachable` rules, which check only `local` and `package` modules.

path.description: Globs that the target of the dependency must match.

reachable.description: `to` is reachable from `from` through other modules.

relation.description: How `to` relates to `from`. A dependency matches when it has any of these relations.

typeOnly.description: The dependency is only `import type` or `export type`.

anyOf.description: Globs the dependency's target must match.
An object with conditions on the dependency and its target.

VisibilityFolder.description: One entry of `folders`: a folder and what it shows to the code outside it.

message.description: Oxcruise shows this text instead of the generic message.

path.description:
Globs of the folders. `{name}` captures a path segment, and `public` and `private` can use
the capture. A glob matches only the folder it names. `**` matches every folder.

private.description:
Globs of the modules in the folder that code outside it cannot import. A glob is relative
to the folder. `private` wins over `public`.

public.description:
Globs of the modules in the folder that code outside it can import. A glob is relative to
the folder. Without `public`, every module is public.

$schema.description: The URL or path of the JSON schema, for editors.

calls.description: Names of functions whose first string argument is a dependency, for example `jest.mock`.

categories.description:
The level of each category of built-in rules. The categories are `correctness`, `suspicious`,
`style` and `restriction`. The default is `correctness: error, suspicious: warn`.

doNotFollow.description: Globs of modules that stay in the graph. Oxcruise does not parse their imports.

entries.description: Files, directories or globs where the graph starts. The default is `["."]`.

extends.description: Paths to other config files. Their settings are the base, and this file changes them.

ignorePatterns.description: Globs of modules to leave out of the graph. Oxcruise also uses the rules of `.gitignore` when it looks for modules.

jsPlugins.description: JS or TS plugins: paths or package names.

overrides.description: Settings that change rules for some modules.

symbols.description:
Extract exports and the names that each import uses, for `json` output and plugins.
Rules that need them enable this option.
